claims.claim: GRASP Layer-12 representations encode specific metal-chelating substructures for MMP inhibition beyond simple molecular weight.
claims.evidence: In tox21/SR-MMP high-noise re-run (resid_mean_10seeds_l12), GRASP mean AUROC=0.880±0.01, while Size baseline is 0.625±0.068 and Morgan fingerprints are 0.754±0.025.
claims.test: SMARTS: [C](=[O])[OH] (hydroxamate zinc-binding group). If true, masking these substructures in test set should drop GRASP AUROC >10% more than Size baseline.
claims.prediction: GRASP prediction probability for masked molecules drops significantly; Size baseline remains unchanged as MW is preserved.

claims.claim: Layer depth correlates with improved discrimination of steroid-like androgen receptor ligands.
claims.evidence: For tox21/NR-AR-LBD mean_pool, GRASP AUROC increases from Layer 4 (0.794±0.081) to Layer 6 (0.813±0.083) to Layer 12 (0.820±0.054).
claims.test: Label: 'is_steroid' derived from RDKit SMARTS [C@H]1CC[C@@H](O)...[ring system]. If true, attention variance on steroid cores should increase in L6/L12 vs L4.
claims.prediction: Attention maps at Layer 12 show higher entropy reduction over fused ring systems compared to Layer 4.

claims.claim: GRASP captures electrophilic toxicophores for ARE activation independent of scaffold split noise.
claims.evidence: In tox21/SR-ARE high-noise re-run (resid_mean_10seeds_l12), GRASP mean AUROC=0.793±0.029 across 10 seeds, significantly outperforming Size baseline (0.609±0.019) and Morgan fingerprints (0.671±0.018).
claims.test: SMARTS: [C](=[O])[CH] or Michael acceptors ([N-]=[N+]=CC=C). If true, removing these motifs should reduce GRASP AUROC more than Bag-of-Words (which counts atoms but ignores topology).
claims.prediction: GRASP performance drops >0.15 AUROC upon motif removal; Bag baseline drops <0.05.

claims.claim: Pretrained weights capture generalizable toxicity signals comparable to fine-tuned models on high-noise tasks.
claims.evidence: In tox21/SR-MMP, GRASP L12 mean=0.889±0.012 (original) and 0.880±0.01 (high noise), while A1_step1 is 0.834±0.022 (original). The gap between pretrained GRASP and fine-tuned baselines narrows in high-noise re-runs.
claims.test: Compare attention heads on known toxicophores across seeds. If true, top-5% predictive molecules overlap >80% between GRASP L12 and A1_step1 despite different training objectives.
claims.prediction: Jaccard similarity of high-confidence positive predictions between GRASP and A1_step1 exceeds 0.7.

claims.claim: GRASP does not rely solely on heavy atom count or molecular weight for toxicity classification.
claims.evidence: In tox21/NR-AR mean_pool, Size baseline AUROC=0.628±0.108 while GRASP L4=0.74±0.085 and Morgan=0.703±0.088. In SR-MMP high-noise re-run, Size=0.625 vs GRASP=0.88.
claims.test: Control: Molecules with matched MW but different scaffolds (e.g., isomers). If true, GRASP AUROC on these pairs should differ significantly while Size baseline remains constant at 1.0 for the pair.
claims.prediction: GRASP predicts opposite classes for structural isomers; Size model assigns identical scores.

trivial_explanations: The 'Size' baseline performance (e.g., NR-AR mean=0.628) indicates that molecular weight alone provides a weak signal, ruling out trivial size-bias as the primary driver of GRASP's success.
For SR-MMP and SR-p53, high AUROC (>0.85) suggests these tasks have strong structural determinants (e.g., zinc-binding groups for MMPs), which graph topology captures better than fixed fingerprints.
